p1.key: Isotopes of the same element have the same number of protons (same atomic number) but different numbers of neutrons, and so different mass numbers: I only.
The peak at 20 is much the most abundant, with smaller peaks at 21 and 22, so the weighted average lies between 20.0 and 21.0, close to 20.
16 protons makes it sulfur. Mass number = 16 + 17 = 33. With 18 electrons (2 more than the protons) the charge is 2−: 33S2−.
1H: 1 electron, 0 neutrons, so yes. 35Cl−: 18 electrons, 18 neutrons, so equal. 39K+: 18 electrons, 20 neutrons, so fewer. I only.
Positive ions are deflected towards the negative plate (paths III and IV). The lighter ion (M) is deflected more (IV) and the heavier M + 2 ion less (III).

p1.key: Peaks at 60, 61 (largest) and 62 (smallest). Weighting gives an average of about 60.9, which is between 60 and 61. The ions are positive, the lightest ion is deflected most, and 61 is a mass number, not a neutron count.
Deflection in a mass spectrometer depends on the mass-to-charge ratio (m/z), so separation depends on both the mass and the charge of the ions.

p1.key: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. X and Y both have 12 protons (12 and 13 neutrons). Electron numbers don't matter (W and Z are ions).
A<sub>r</sub> = 63.55 is much closer to 63 than 65, so <sup>63</sup>Cu must be the main isotope. Check: 0.70 × 63 + 0.30 × 65 = 63.6.
Isotopes are atoms of the same element: same atomic (proton) number but different numbers of neutrons, so different mass numbers.
In a mass spectrometer the sample is vaporized, ionized (to form positive ions), accelerated by an electric field, then deflected by a magnetic field and detected.

p1.key: Mg has atomic number 12, so 12 protons; neutrons = 26 − 12 = 14; the 2+ ion has lost 2 electrons, leaving 12 − 2 = 10.
Ar = (0.60 × 69) + (0.40 × 71) = 41.4 + 28.4 = 69.8, closer to 69 because that isotope is more abundant.
Mg has 12 electrons as an atom (atomic number 12); the 2+ ion has lost two, leaving 10. The mass number 24 is not needed.
Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. W and Z both have 18 protons, with 22 and 20 neutrons.
Oxygen has 8 protons, so neutrons = 18 − 8 = 10. The 2− charge changes the number of electrons, not neutrons.
Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. L and Q both have 12 protons, with 12 and 14 neutrons. P is an ion of M (same protons and neutrons, fewer electrons).
In a (traditional) mass spectrometer atoms are ionized by electron bombardment, accelerated by an electric field, then deflected by a magnetic field. So II is wrong.

p1.key: Ar = (28 × 20 + 29 × 80) ÷ 100 = (560 + 2320) ÷ 100 = 28.8. The mean lies closer to 29 because that isotope is more abundant.
The sample is first vaporized, then ionized (e.g. electron bombardment), accelerated by an electric field, and deflected by a magnetic field before detection.

p1.key: Both are copper, so both have 29 protons. 63Cu2+ has 27 electrons and 34 neutrons; 65Cu+ has 28 electrons and 36 neutrons, so B, C and D are false.
All chlorine atoms have 17 protons (that defines the element) and, being neutral, 17 electrons. Neutron numbers differ between isotopes (<sup>35</sup>Cl has 18, <sup>37</sup>Cl has 20).
Ar = (24 × 80 + 25 × 10 + 26 × 10) ÷ 100 = 24.3, which lies between 24 and 25, closer to 24 because 24X is most abundant.
Atomic number 9 is fluorine; mass number 19 goes top-left: <sup>19</sup><sub>9</sub>F. K and Si have atomic numbers 19 and 14.
Deflection depends on mass/charge: the smaller m/z, the greater the deflection. 35Cl2+ has m/z = 17.5, the lowest of the four.
The sample is first vaporized, then ionized to form positive ions. The ions are accelerated by an electric field, deflected by a magnetic field according to m/z, and finally detected.

p1.key: Iodine has atomic number 53, so neutrons = 125 − 53 = 72. The 1+ ion has lost one electron, so it has 53 − 1 = 52 electrons.
Deflection is proportional to charge/mass ratio. <sup>16</sup>O<sup>2+</sup> has the largest m/z ratio of 2/16, so it is deflected most; <sup>18</sup>O<sup>+</sup> (1/18) is deflected least.

p1.key: Atomic number 24 = 24 protons (and 24 electrons in the atom). Mass number 53 = 53 nucleons, so neutrons = 53 − 24 = 29.
Mass number = 31 + 40 = 71, atomic number = 31, and 31 protons − 28 electrons gives a 3+ charge: 7131Z3+.
Iodine has atomic number 53, so it has 53 protons. Neutrons = mass number − protons = 131 − 53 = 78.
Z = 16, so 16 protons. Neutrons = 34 − 16 = 18. The 2− charge means two extra electrons: 16 + 2 = 18 electrons.
A 2− charge means the atom has two more electrons than protons, i.e. it has gained two electrons. Protons are never gained or lost when ions form.
